title: Executors.newFixedThreadPool is dangerous — unbounded queue OOM, use ThreadPoolExecutor instead

s1_definition.profdef: `Executors.newFixedThreadPool(n)` creates a `ThreadPoolExecutor` with an **unbounded** `LinkedBlockingQueue` (capacity = `Integer.MAX_VALUE`). Under sustained overload: producers submit faster than workers process → tasks accumulate indefinitely → each `Runnable` occupies heap memory → millions of queued tasks → **OutOfMemoryError**! No rejection ever fires (queue never "full"). The JVM crashes. Similarly dangerous: `newCachedThreadPool()` (unbounded THREADS — can create millions), `newSingleThreadExecutor()` (unbounded queue). **Fix**: use `ThreadPoolExecutor` directly with a BOUNDED `LinkedBlockingQueue(capacity)` and a rejection handler. Alibaba's Java coding guidelines and SonarQube both flag `Executors` factory methods as violations.
s1_definition.analogy: `newFixedThreadPool` = 10 tellers with an INFINITE waiting line. 100K customers arrive → all wait in line → line fills the ENTIRE building → building collapses (OOM). Nobody was ever turned away (no rejection) → so the building kept accepting more until it couldn't hold them. Fix: waiting line capped at 500 → 501st customer: "Sorry, come back later!" Building survives.
s1_definition.oneliner: newFixedThreadPool = unbounded queue → OOM under load. newCachedThreadPool = unbounded threads → OOM. ALWAYS: new ThreadPoolExecutor(core, max, queue=BOUNDED, handler). Alibaba/SonarQube: Executors factory = code smell!
s1_definition.raw:
**Professional definition:** `Executors.newFixedThreadPool(n)` creates a `ThreadPoolExecutor` with an **unbounded** `LinkedBlockingQueue` (capacity = `Integer.MAX_VALUE`). Under sustained overload: producers submit faster than workers process → tasks accumulate indefinitely → each `Runnable` occupies heap memory → millions of queued tasks → **OutOfMemoryError**! No rejection ever fires (queue never "full"). The JVM crashes. Similarly dangerous: `newCachedThreadPool()` (unbounded THREADS — can create millions), `newSingleThreadExecutor()` (unbounded queue). **Fix**: use `ThreadPoolExecutor` directly with a BOUNDED `LinkedBlockingQueue(capacity)` and a rejection handler. Alibaba's Java coding guidelines and SonarQube both flag `Executors` factory methods as violations.

**In simple words (banking analogy):** `newFixedThreadPool` = 10 tellers with an INFINITE waiting line. 100K customers arrive → all wait in line → line fills the ENTIRE building → building collapses (OOM). Nobody was ever turned away (no rejection) → so the building kept accepting more until it couldn't hold them. Fix: waiting line capped at 500 → 501st customer: "Sorry, come back later!" Building survives.

**One line to remember:** newFixedThreadPool = unbounded queue → OOM under load. newCachedThreadPool = unbounded threads → OOM. ALWAYS: new ThreadPoolExecutor(core, max, queue=BOUNDED, handler). Alibaba/SonarQube: Executors factory = code smell!

sections.s3_banking: **Problem — The statement generation service used `Executors.newFixedThreadPool(5)`.** Monthly batch: 2M statements. 5 workers processing at 100/sec = 20,000 seconds for 2M. Task submission: 10,000/sec. Queue growth: 9,900/sec. After 5 minutes: 3M tasks queued × 2KB each = 6GB heap → OOM → service crash → monthly statements delayed 2 days. Fix: `ThreadPoolExecutor(5, 10, 60s, LinkedBlockingQueue(10000), CallerRunsPolicy)`. Queue capped at 10K. CallerRuns: producer thread (batch scheduler) slows down naturally. OOM eliminated. Statements completed in 6 hours (batch scheduler regulated by back-pressure).

sections.s5_journey:
**Step 1.** `newFixedThreadPool(1)` + 10,000 tasks. 1 worker processes 1 task/sec. Queue: 9,999 tasks × ~2KB = ~20MB. In production: millions of tasks × KB each → GB → OOM!

**Step 2.** Bounded queue(100) + rejection handler. 1 worker + 100 queued = 101 accepted. 9,899 REJECTED immediately. Memory: constant ~200KB. No OOM!

**Step 3.** `newCachedThreadPool()` + 1000 tasks. 1000 threads created! Each thread: ~1MB stack = 1GB stack memory. In production: 100K tasks → 100K threads → 100GB → OOM!

sections.s6_takeaway:
`Executors.newFixedThreadPool()` is dangerous in production: it uses an UNBOUNDED `LinkedBlockingQueue` (capacity = Integer.MAX_VALUE). Under sustained overload, tasks pile up indefinitely → millions of Runnables in the queue → heap exhausted → `OutOfMemoryError`. No rejection ever fires because the queue never "fills up." Similarly: `newCachedThreadPool()` creates unbounded THREADS (up to Integer.MAX_VALUE). Both are OOM time bombs.

Fix: use `ThreadPoolExecutor` directly with BOUNDED queue: `new LinkedBlockingQueue<>(500)`. When full: rejection handler fires (CallerRunsPolicy for back-pressure, or custom handler with Prometheus metrics + logging). Alibaba Java Coding Guidelines and SonarQube both flag Executors factory methods as code violations. In banking: statement generation with `newFixedThreadPool(5)` → 3M tasks queued → 6GB heap → OOM → 2-day delay. After: `ThreadPoolExecutor` with bounded(10K) + CallerRunsPolicy → 6-hour completion, zero OOM.
